proposal: Add WP-243 coverage-contract blocks for the three wholesale winter sports that today have NO mechanical catch — alpine, cross-country (langrenn) and biathlon (skiskyting) — by seeding their verdenscup competitions into scripts/config/authority.json (authority fis/ibu + skiforbundet/skiskytterforbundet for time, NRK for channel) with a conservative des–feb contract (horizonDays 28, minUpcoming 1, months [12,1,2]). Ski jumping (hopp) is deliberately deferred: catalog tier1 keys it as 'ski jumping' (space), which breaks authority.schema's sport pattern and is unconfirmed against events.json's sport key — a key-normalization question that should not be guessed under auto-merge.
evidence: coverage-audit.json 2026-11-02 top sourceIssue (severity HIGH, 'STRUKTURELT, ROT-ÅRSAK for fire horisont-hull'): alpint/hopp/langrenn/skiskyting are all catalog-tier1 (wholesale) but have NO static fetcher AND no authority.json contract-block, so the whole winter season is hand-boarded race-by-race and four opening gaps sit in the horizon with no mechanical catch. The audit itself names the fix: 'Argument (HIGH, stigende når vinteren topper seg des–mars) for en FIS/IBU-fetcher ELLER authority.json contract-blokker for alpint/hopp/langrenn/skiskyting-VC … Self-repair/improve-sak.'

coverage-audit.json gaps: alpint (recurrences 6), hopp (recurrences 9), langrenn (recurrences 5), skiskyting (recurrences 2) — all carry-forward since 24–31.10, all MEDIUM held deliberately because research boards on cadence, but the recurrence counts show the reliance-on-cadence is fragile and the root cause is the missing mechanical guarantee.

coverage-audit.json coveredWell DEKNINGSKONTRAKTER note: 'NB: ingen contract-blokk for vintersport, håndball, EL/ECL, CS2 eller sykkel — derfor fanges ikke de hullene mekanisk; se sourceIssues.' — the absence of a winter contract is explicitly called out as why these gaps are not caught mechanically.
research-log.json 2026-11-02 quality.failures carry-forward: 'strukturelle fetcher-mangler … FIS/IBU vintersport-fetcher … routet til self-repair/improve'.

The fix leverages EXISTING WP-243 machinery (scripts/lib/coverage-contracts.js + detect-coverage-gaps contract-breach signal + port-report contracts port) — it is config/data, not new machinery, matching the improve bias ('sharpen what exists over adding machinery'). The required sources already exist in sources.json with the correct roles (fis/ibu = federation & authoritative for the sports; skiforbundet/skiskytterforbundet = federation; nrk = official-broadcaster).

Conservative contract numbers (per authority.schema's heavy false-breach warning): scoped to the DENSE CORE des–feb only, horizonDays 28 + minUpcoming 1. Simulated: on 2026-11-02 all three evaluate 'off-season' (NO breach — zero disruption to the agents' current Nov cadence handling / medium-hold of the openings); simulated on 2027-01-15 with a dark board they correctly 'breach'. The ragged season edges (Sölden/Levi Nov openings, mars finals) are deliberately outside months and stay the recall-gaps/coverage-critic job (hard frists), avoiding the Nov-start and late-March false-breach edges.

npm test: 88 files / 1546 tests pass, incl. tests/authority-schema.test.js (schema, id-sort, role doctrine, sport-authority, lowercase match patterns). authority.json round-trips byte-identically with tab indent so the diff is minimal (108 insertions).
expectedEffect: From 1 December each winter, if the board goes silently dark for alpine, cross-country or biathlon for 28+ days during peak season (a real coverage failure — no static fetcher backstops these wholesale sports), the WP-243 contract mechanically fires a HIGH contract-breach gap that coverage-critic/research triage and that colours the port-report contracts port (G2). This is a durable recall FLOOR for the winter core that nothing provides today; completeness/speed of individual race boarding stays the agents' job. No behaviour change in November (off-season per the contract).
howWeKnow: coverage-contracts.json should show the three winter contracts as 'off-season' through November, flip to 'met' once research boards the dense Dec season, and 'breached' only if a winter sport genuinely falls off the board mid-winter. If any winter contract breaches during Nov–Feb while coverage is actually healthy, the months/horizon were too aggressive and should be widened (as the Eliteserien minUpcoming 4→2 and PGA 14→21 tunings did earlier).
notes: Chose this over: (a) schedule tuning — usage-summary 7d avg 9% / peak 17%, 30d avg 11% / peak 45%, 0 amber/red hours, so quota is healthy and no cron change is warranted; (b) the actively-breaking self-repair items (Playwright ubuntu-26.04 runner pin, research-agent allowed_bots, visual-qa --max-turns) — all live in .github/workflows/**, a protected path CI agents may not author (blocked by protect-automation.js), owner-only; (c) a new FIS/IBU fetcher — new machinery, against the v2 bias, and the contract-block delivers the recall guarantee without it.

Deferred ski jumping (hopp) intentionally — see proposal. Handball, EL/ECL, CS2 and cycling contract-blocks are the same class of fix and are good follow-ups, but one focused improvement per run; winter had the strongest multi-signal evidence (HIGH sourceIssue + four recurring gaps + in-season now).
